editorial.headline: Metal Finishing With a Clean National and Bali Signal
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25920 covers specialist metal working and coating services, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25920 is the industrial code for metal working and metal coating: the practical, often invisible layer of production that turns metal parts into finished, treated, cleaned, strengthened, polished, joined, or marked components. The record describes a broad workshop and service field: plating, anodizing, heat treatment, deburring, sandblasting, tumbling, cleaning, colouring, engraving, non-metal coatings such as plastic, enamel, porcelain, lacquer, and varnish, hardening, polishing, welding, joining, sawing, grinding, drilling, shaping, sharpening, and laser cutting or writing on metal. In plain English, this is not the making of every metal object from scratch; it is the specialist processing, finishing, preparation, repair, and treatment of metal and metal products.

The commercial profile is deliberately wide. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses, so it can describe a small finishing shop, a mid-sized industrial service provider, or a larger operation serving manufacturing clients. That breadth matters because the activity is defined by the process applied to metal rather than by one narrow end product. A founder registering under this code should therefore read the scope around the actual services performed: coating, cleaning, polishing, engraving, welding, cutting, heat treatment, and other specific metal-working services are the centre of gravity.

Nationally, the signal is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the record gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, with Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 as the PMA source. That means the national record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no licence, capital threshold, timeline, tax rule, or operating permit stated in the slim record, so none should be inferred from the classification itself. The safe reading is narrower and cleaner: as a national investment classification, this activity is open to PMA up to the percentage stated in the record.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a different reason. The record marks Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says it is not blocked. Its reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium text in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not treated here as blocked by that rule. So the honest lede is not a warning that Bali shuts it down. For this record, KBLI 25920 is nationally open to foreign ownership and, on the Bali-specific fields provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
